objective: Evaluating stakeholder-identified risks and incorporating them into the program risk management plan
secondaryObjectives: Negotiating stakeholder support and setting clear expectations and acceptance criteria (e.g., KPIs) for program benefits
Performing stakeholder analysis (historical data, interviews, formal agreements) to build a stakeholder engagement plan

sources.cite: PMI, Program Management Professional (PgMP) Examination Content Outline: Strategic Program Alignment 15%, Program Life Cycle Management 44%, Benefits Management 11%, Stakeholder Engagement 16%, Governance 14%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17. The domain weights were confirmed through a summarizing fetch of a training provider's article (eartech.pmtraining.com, 'How to Prepare for the PgMP Certification Exam'), which describes Program Life Cycle Management as 'initiating, planning, executing, controlling, and closing the program across its phases' and Governance as 'the boards, gates, and decision rights that let leadership steer and, when needed, stop a program'. PMI's own outline PDF did not come up in search and PMI's PgMP pages read today do not list the domains; the task wording is the course seed's, to verify against PMI's PDF. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's pgmp-transit-program-steering-review (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the portfolio or program, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You run the paperless wards program at St Anselm's Health, a fictional hospital trust: four projects over two years. Clinical staff, the nurses' union and IT all have concerns.
handover: Nurses' union: worried about charting time at the bedside.
The program's benefits: fewer medication errors and 20 minutes saved per nurse per shift.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a fortnight at a time. A decision comes to you at each board meeting; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Meeting 2: the pilot ward's dead spots stop bedside charting; nurses revert to paper and the union calls for a halt.

risksPrompt.title: Concerns or risks?
risksPrompt.context: Three concerns came from the interviews.

choices.label: Evaluate each concern as a program risk (winter go-live, charting time, Wi-Fi dead spots), with owners and responses in the program risk register
choices.feedback: Stakeholders see risks the plan doesn't; evaluating and registering them makes them managed.

choices.label: Record them as stakeholder feedback
choices.feedback: Feedback with no owner or response isn't managed.

choices.label: Dismiss them as resistance to change
choices.feedback: The concerns were real risks; dismissing them loses stakeholders too.

choices.label: Agree KPIs with the groups: medication error rate, charting minutes per shift measured on pilot wards, and a no-worse-than-paper criterion for go-live

effects.log: Shared KPIs and a go-live criterion are agreed.

choices.feedback: Negotiated, measurable acceptance criteria align expectations.

choices.label: Promise 'a better experience for everyone'
choices.feedback: Nothing to accept or measure; expectations diverge.

supPrompt.title: Winter go-live
supPrompt.context: The sponsor wants go-live in January; ward managers and the union oppose it.

choices.label: Bring the evidence (winter risk, pilot KPIs) to the sponsor and ward managers and agree a March go-live with super-users on each ward

effects.log: A March go-live with super-users is agreed.

choices.feedback: Engagement based on shared evidence keeps support for the program.

choices.label: Go live in January on two wards only
choices.feedback: A compromise, but still in the riskiest weeks.

choices.label: Hold January: the sponsor decides
choices.feedback: Overriding clinical stakeholders repeats the last program's failure.

reflection.question: Write the stakeholder engagement note for the program board.

parts.label: Risks and expectations
parts.criteria: Three concerns registered with owners; KPIs and a go-live criterion agreed.
parts.modelAnswer: Winter go-live, charting time and Wi-Fi dead spots are program risks with owners; we agreed KPIs for errors and charting minutes and a no-worse-than-paper criterion.

parts.label: Support
parts.criteria: A March go-live with super-users agreed on evidence.
parts.modelAnswer: Using the pilot data and last program's lessons, the sponsor and ward managers agreed a March go-live with super-users.

scoring.modelReasoning: Program stakeholders identify risks the plan misses; evaluating their concerns and incorporating them in the program risk management plan makes them managed. Negotiated, measurable acceptance criteria (KPIs) align expectations for benefits. Support is sustained by shaping key decisions with stakeholders on shared evidence.
